parameters.content:
VIDEO VERSION — faithful reconstruction from the source evidence.
Source: https://www.instagram.com/_no_hype_ai/reel/Da0EUZAu0ve/
Evidence: [0.16s - 23.72s] [Speaker 0] So this is how I add ideas and reminders to my Obsidian second brain no matter where I am. So first thing I'll do, I'll pop open the Obsidian widget that I have on my phone, and I'll just dictate whatever the thought is straight into it. Something like add tomatoes to my grocery list. That'll kick off an automation, which will try to classify the note that I just dropped in the inbox. It'll determine if it's an idea, a to do list item, a resource to remember, or a project idea.
[24.18s - 33.43s] [Speaker 0] Once it classifies it, it will then clean up the text within the document and restructure so that it fits neatly into my second brain. Links, tags, etcetera.
[33.89s - 62.35s] [Speaker 0] Once it's in the second brain, what happens when I wanna access it? Well, that's where I have a Telegram agent that has full read write access to the entire Obsidian vault. So if I ask that agent something like, hey, what's on my to do list for today? It'll say, call dentist, buy tomatoes, etcetera. And if I say something like, I already bought tomatoes, please remove that. It can then update that file, and then resync it to the vault, so that the second brain is always up to date. I like this because I always have my best ideas when I'm not in front of my computer.
[62.97s - 73.14s] [Speaker 0] And if you're interested, the workflow is nearly released. So comment workflow, and I will send it to you. And let me know if you want deeper dives into this particular workflow.
Source-vs-engineering boundary: NEXEN/MARVIN searchable memory conventions, deterministic note IDs, duplicate suppression and append-only review audit. Telegram write credentials remain to bind.
No external side effects are enabled on import.
